mainTopic: Orphans and פרוזבול, חנן בישא's slaps, and an ox that is מועד for only some victims, with the debate over 'ואינו מועד' and 'אינו מועד'
overview: The amud opens at the end of a statement that orphans do not need a פרוזבול, and רמי בר חמא explains why: בית דין acts as the father of orphans. Next comes a short story. חנן בישא was fined half a זוז for a slap, could not get change for his damaged coin, and so slapped the man again and handed over the whole coin. A new משנה then teaches that an ox can be מועד toward one type of victim or on one day, such as שבת, and still be a תם for everything else. In the גמרא, רב זביד and רב פפא argue whether the משנה reads 'ואינו מועד' or 'אינו מועד'. That one letter decides whether an ordinary ox that is מועד for its own kind counts as מועד for other kinds too. Each side proves his reading from a different line of the משנה, and each answers the other's proof. רב זביד also answers a challenge from סומכוס, and רב אשי and רב ינאי bring further support for him. The גמרא rules that an ox which gored an ox, a donkey and a camel is מועד for all of them, even according to רב פפא. Two ברייתות then teach about an ox that gores every other animal, and a new question begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Orphans do not need a פרוזבול
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a statement already in progress: orphans do not need a פרוזבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Orphans] do not need a פרוזבול.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a sentence that began on the previous עמוד. It rules that orphans do not need a פרוזבול to protect the loans owed to them from being cancelled by שמיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally שמיטה cancels loans unless the lender writes a פרוזבול, which hands the right to collect over to בית דין. Orphans are an exception: בית דין already looks after their property, so their loans count as if they were already handed to the court.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that hands a loan over to בית דין so that שמיטה does not cancel it
They do not need
Orphans

phrases.english: do not need a prosbul.
phrases.notes: This is about orphans, who were mentioned just before this, at the end of the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans' loans are not cancelled by שמיטה even without a פרוזבול.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא supports the rule about orphans
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא teaches the same rule and gives the reason: רבן גמליאל and his court were the fathers of orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רמי בר חמא taught: orphans do not need a פרוזבול, because רבן גמליאל and his court were the fathers of orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that matches the rule we just heard. It also gives the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וכן תני' tell us this is support for the earlier statement, not a new argument. The reason is that בית דין stands in the place of a father for orphans and looks after their money. A loan owed to orphans is therefore already in the court's hands, and that is exactly what a פרוזבול would have done.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too [someone] taught; this brings support
His court
The fathers of orphans; the ones responsible for them

steps.whatToRemember: Orphans do not need a פרוזבול because בית דין is treated as their guardian, so their loans already count as being in the court's hands.

phrases.english: And so too Rami bar Chama taught:
Orphans do not need a prosbul,
[because] Rabban Gamliel and his court
were the fathers of orphans.
phrases.notes: In other words, the court took care of orphans' affairs the way a father would.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 and explains its reason.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that orphans do not need a פרוזבול
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רמי בר חמא, based on בית דין being the father of orphans

steps.title: רב הונא sets the fine for a slap
steps.stepSummary: חנן בישא slapped a man, and רב הונא ordered him to pay half a זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן the wicked slapped a certain man. He came before רב הונא, who told him: go give him half a זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. It shows the fine for slapping someone being put into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slapping a person carries a fixed fine called בושת, a payment for the embarrassment. Here רב הונא rules that the amount is half a זוז. The next step shows how חנן responded.

keyTerms.meaning: He slapped him
Go give him
Half a זוז (a coin)

phrases.english: Chanan the wicked
phrases.notes: בִּישָׁא means 'bad' or 'wicked.' It is a nickname, and the story shows why he earned it.

phrases.english: slapped a certain man.
He came before Rav Huna.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל הַב לֵיהּ פַּלְגָא דְזוּזָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Go give him half a zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָנָן בִּישָׁא תְּקַע לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the orphans topic to a story about the fine for a slap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fine for a slap is half a זוז.

steps.title: חנן slaps again to use up his coin
steps.stepSummary: חנן had only a damaged whole זוז that nobody would break into change, so he slapped the man again and handed over the whole coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a damaged זוז and wanted to give half a זוז from it, but nobody would take it to make change. So he slapped him again and gave him the coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with חנן's nasty solution. Since he could not get change, he gave a second slap so that he would owe a full זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two slaps add up to two half-זוז fines, which equals one whole זוז. Instead of finding change, חנן simply 'used up' the rest of his coin with another slap. This shows how a fixed fine can be cynically taken advantage of, and why he was called 'the wicked.'

keyTerms.meaning: A worn or damaged זוז
Nobody would take it from him
Another one

steps.whatToRemember: Each slap carries its own fixed fine of half a זוז, so חנן's second slap made him owe a whole זוז.

phrases.english: He had a damaged zuz.
phrases.notes: מָכָא means worn or chipped, so it was hard to get anyone to break it into change.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי לְמִיתְּבֵהּ לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ פַּלְגָא דְּזוּזָא,
phrases.english: He wanted to give him half a zuz out of it,
but nobody would take it from him.
So he slapped him another [time],
and gave it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each slap is its own fine, so two slaps add up to a full זוז.

steps.title: An ox forewarned for only some victims
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: an ox can be מועד for one kind of victim and תם for another. It pays נזק שלם for the kind it is מועד to and חצי נזק for the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An ox that is forewarned for its own kind but not for other kinds, forewarned for people but not for animals, or forewarned for small ones but not for large ones: for the kind it is forewarned for, the owner pays full damage, and for the kind it is not forewarned for, he pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that being מועד can apply to just one type of victim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox becomes מועד by goring several times. This משנה says that status is tied to the type of victim it has been goring, such as its own species, people, or small animals. Toward that type the owner pays נזק שלם. Toward any other type the ox is still treated as a תם, and the owner pays only חצי נזק.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; a new משנה starts here
Forewarned; an ox with a history of goring, whose owner pays full damage
Toward its own kind (species)
Full damage payment
Half damage payment, as for a תם

steps.whatToRemember: Being מועד is not all-or-nothing. An ox can be מועד toward one type of victim and still be a תם toward every other type.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think an ox is simply either מועד or תם for everything. The משנה ties the status to a specific type of victim, so the same ox can pay נזק שלם in one case and חצי נזק in another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming גמרא discussion about how specific a מועד status can be.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
An ox that is forewarned toward its own kind,
but is not forewarned toward what is not its kind;
forewarned toward people
but not forewarned toward animals;
forewarned toward small ones
but not forewarned toward large ones;

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁהוּא מוּעָד לוֹ – מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
phrases.english: toward what it is forewarned, [the owner] pays full damage,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּעָד לוֹ – מְשַׁלֵּם חֲצִי נֶזֶק.
phrases.english: and toward what it is not forewarned, he pays half damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox's מועד status applies only to the type of victim it has been goring. It pays נזק שלם for that type and חצי נזק for all others.

steps.title: The Sages ask about an ox that gores only on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask רבי יהודה what the law is for an ox that is מועד on שבת but not on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to רבי יהודה: What if this ox is מועד for שבתות but not מועד for weekdays?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case, an ox that is a known gorer only on שבת. The Sages ask רבי יהודה what to do with it, and this sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 taught that an ox can be מועד for one kind of victim and תם for another. This question pushes the same idea into time: can an ox be מועד on certain days only?

keyTerms.meaning: An ox with a proven habit of goring. Its owner pays full damage.
For the days of שבת
Weekdays, the ordinary days that are not שבת
The תנא the Sages are asking

phrases.english: They said before Rabbi Yehuda:
If this ox is forewarned for Shabbatot
but is not forewarned for weekdays, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries step 5's idea of partial מועד status over from kinds of victims to days of the week.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much the owner pays for an ox that is מועד only on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: full damage on שבת, half on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that the owner pays נזק שלם for goring on שבת and חצי נזק for goring on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: For שבתות, he pays full damage. For weekdays, he pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question from step 6. The ox counts as מועד on שבת and as תם on weekdays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule follows the same pattern as step 5: you pay full damage where the ox is מועד and half damage where it is תם. Here the dividing line is the day of the week, not the kind of victim.

keyTerms.meaning: Full payment for the damage, the rule for a מועד
Half payment for the damage, the rule for a תם
The weekdays

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לַשַּׁבָּתוֹת – מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
phrases.english: He said to them: For Shabbatot, he pays full damage,
for weekdays, he pays half damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Sages' question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Full damage for goring on שבת, half damage for goring on weekdays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox can be מועד for certain days only and is treated as תם on the other days.

steps.title: When the שבת-goring ox goes back to being תם
steps.stepSummary: The ox loses its שבת מועד status after it stays calm on three שבתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it become תם again? Once it has changed its ways for three שבת days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes this case by explaining how the ox can lose its מועד status. It has to stay calm on three שבתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ox's habit is tied to שבת, it has to show its change on שבת too. Calm weekdays prove nothing, because the ox was always calm on weekdays.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox with no proven habit of goring. Its owner pays half damage.
When?
Once it changes its ways
Three שבת days, one in each of three weeks

steps.whatToRemember: An ox can be מועד for one kind of victim or for one day of the week. Its status goes back to תם only when it shows calm behavior in that same area, here three calm שבתות.

phrases.english: When is it innocuous again?
Once it changes its ways for three days of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהודה's case by explaining how the שבת מועד status ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שבת-only מועד goes back to תם after three calm שבתות.

steps.title: רב זביד and רב פפא argue over one letter in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with an argument over whether the משנה says 'and is not מועד' (with a ו) or just 'is not מועד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב זביד said, 'and is not מועד' is what we learned. רב פפא said, 'is not מועד' is what we learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by going back to the line from step 5, 'מועד for its own kind and not מועד for other kinds.' Two אמוראים disagree about its exact wording, and this sets up the next step, which explains why that wording matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two readings is the letter ו. The next step shows that this one letter changes the rule for an ordinary ox.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here
It was stated, which opens a debate between אמוראים
We learned in the משנה
An אמורא who reads the word with a ו
An אמורא who reads the word without a ו

steps.confusionAlert: They are not arguing about the שבת case just mentioned. They are arguing about the earlier line on kinds of animals, 'מועד for its own kind' (step 5).

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav Zevid said: We learned 'and is not forewarned.'
phrases.notes: The whole argument is about one letter: does the משנה from step 5 say 'and is not' (with a ו) or just 'is not'?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: We learned 'is not forewarned.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by going back to the wording of the משנה line in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב זביד reads 'ואינו מועד' and רב פפא reads 'אינו מועד.'

steps.title: What each reading means for an ordinary ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that for רב זביד, an ordinary ox that is מועד for its own kind is מועד for all kinds. For רב פפא, it is not מועד for other kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said 'and is not מועד': this implies that in a plain case it is מועד. רב פפא said 'is not מועד': in a plain case it is not מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion and spells out what it means for a regular ox that nobody has specially checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ו, the משנה describes one special case, an ox shown to be calm with other kinds. That suggests an ordinary ox is מועד for everything. Without the ו, the משנה states a general rule: being מועד for one kind does not make an ox מועד for other kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, ordinary case with no special facts
This implies
Is, counts as

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד: an ordinary ox that is מועד for its own kind is מועד for all kinds. רב פפא: an ordinary ox is מועד only for the kind it has proven to gore.
steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement decides whether the owner of an ordinary ox pays full or half damage when it gores a different kind of animal.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said we learned 'and is not forewarned':
this implies that in an ordinary case it is forewarned.
phrases.notes: 'Ordinary case' means nobody has shown that the ox stays calm around other kinds of animals.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said we learned 'is not forewarned':
meaning that in an ordinary case it is not forewarned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the two readings from step 9 to show what each one means in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב זביד: an ordinary ox is מועד for all kinds. רב פפא: an ordinary ox is not מועד for other kinds.

steps.title: Each opinion comes from a different part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד bases his reading on the סיפא of the משנה, and רב פפא bases his reading on the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד learns his view from the end of the משנה. רב פפא learns his view from the beginning of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us that each side has a source in the משנה, and the next lines will show each proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only heard what each one holds (Steps 9-10). Now we learn they are not guessing: each reads a different line of the משנה closely. The גמרא will first explain רב זביד's proof from the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns out / makes an inference from a close reading
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
The opening part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rav Zevid infers from the latter clause,
Rav Pappa infers from the first clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד דָּיֵיק מִסֵּיפָא, רַב פָּפָּא דָּיֵיק מֵרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual source behind the two positions explained in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב זביד proves his reading from the סיפא; רב פפא proves his from the רישא.

steps.title: רב זביד's proof: with 'and is not מועד', the later line teaches something new
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא speaks of an ox that is מועד for small animals and not for large ones. If the רישא reads 'and is not מועד', then the default is that the ox is מועד for everything, and the סיפא adds that this is true even from small animals to large ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The end of the משנה says: 'מועד for small ones and not מועד for large ones.' It makes sense if the משנה said 'and is not מועד.' That wording means that normally the ox is מועד for everything. Then the end of the משנה teaches us something new: even going from small animals to large ones, the ox is normally counted as מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד quotes the end of the משנה and shows that it fits well with his reading, 'and is not מועד.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ו, the משנה means the ox is only limited when we actually saw it leave other animals alone. Without that, the default is that it is מועד for all. So the סיפא makes a new and bold point: even an ox that only gored small animals is normally counted as מועד for large ones too, even though large ones are harder to gore.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say (sets up the reading that fits)
The plain, default case, with no special evidence either way
It teaches us (the new point)
Small animals / large animals

phrases.english: Rav Zevid infers from the latter clause –
as it teaches: forewarned for small ones
and not forewarned for large ones.
It makes sense if you say
that it teaches 'and is not forewarned' –
phrases.notes: This goes back to the opening line of the משנה: 'מועד for its own kind, and is not מועד for other kinds.'

phrases.english: then normally it is forewarned;
this teaches us –
that even from small ones to large ones as well,
by default it is forewarned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the proof from the סיפא announced in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's reading 'וְאֵינוֹ מוּעָד': an ox is normally מועד for every kind of animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: 'מועד לקטנים ואינו מועד לגדולים.'

steps.title: Testing רב פפא's reading: the default would be 'not מועד'
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the משנה reads only 'is not מועד', as רב פפא says. Then the plain default is that the ox is not מועד for other kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But suppose you say the משנה reads only 'is not מועד.' Then normally the ox is not counted as מועד for other kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the other reading, 'is not מועד' without the ו. This line sets up the problem that comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the default flips. Without the ו, an ox that is מועד for its own kind is automatically not מועד for other kinds. The next line will show that this makes the סיפא pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say (brings in the other reading)

phrases.english: But if you say
that it teaches 'is not forewarned' –
then normally it is not forewarned,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the reading that fits (Step 12) to the other reading, so it can show the problem with it.
steps.raayaObject: Shows what רב פפא's reading would mean for the default case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opening line of the משנה, read without the ו.

steps.title: Without the ו, the later line of the משנה would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the ox is not even מועד for small animals of other kinds, then of course it is not מועד for large ones. So the סיפא would teach nothing, which proves the משנה must read 'and is not מועד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think it through. If an ox that gored small animals is not normally מועד even for other small animals in general, do we really need to be told that it is not מועד for large ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that shows רב פפא's reading makes the end of the משנה unnecessary. That supports רב זביד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not waste words. Under 'is not מועד', the ox is limited even for other small animals, so it is obviously limited for large ones, and the סיפא would add nothing. Since the סיפא must teach something, the משנה must read 'and is not מועד', as רב זביד says.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (if even the easier case is true)
In general / of the world at large
Does it need to be said? (meaning: it is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד's proof: the סיפא (small to large) only teaches something new if the default is that the ox is מועד for everything. So the משנה must read 'וְאֵינוֹ מוּעָד', with the ו.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though this line is a question, the גמרא is not asking for information. It is pointing out that רב פפא's reading would make the סיפא pointless.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of how the גמרא reads a משנה: every line must teach something, so a reading that makes a line obvious is pushed aside.

phrases.english: Now, if it can be said
that from small ones to small ones in general,
normally it is not forewarned;
from small ones to large ones, need it be said
that it is not forewarned?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר מִקְּטַנִּים לִקְטַנִּים דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the line started in Step 13 by showing that רב פפא's reading makes the סיפא unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of the משנה as 'אֵינוֹ מוּעָד' without the ו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ox is not מועד even for small animals of other kinds, it is obviously not מועד for large ones, so the סיפא would be needless. A משנה does not teach the obvious.

steps.title: רב פפא shows the clause about small and large animals still teaches something
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that even under his reading the סיפא is needed. Without it, we might think that once a שור has 'broken out' against a species, it is מועד for both the big and the small animals of that species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא would answer: the סיפא is needed. You might have thought that since the ox broke out against that species, it has broken out against all of it, big and small alike. So the משנה teaches us that it is not מועד for the large ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his reading against the challenge in Step 14 by showing that the סיפא still adds a new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that under רב פפא's reading the סיפא (small vs. large) is obvious. רב פפא answers that the סיפא is about one and the same species. One could have thought that goring some animals of a species makes the שור dangerous to that whole species, whatever their size. The סיפא teaches that size still matters.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; the clause is not extra
You might have thought; introduces a mistaken assumption
Broke out; the ox broke its normal calm behavior
It teaches us; what the source comes to say

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa would say to you:
It is necessary,
phrases.notes: He means the סיפא about small and large animals is still needed, even with his reading.

phrases.english: because it would have entered your mind to say:
since it broke out against that species,
it has broken out against it completely,
no difference whether its large ones
and no difference whether its small ones;

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא הָוֵי מוּעָד.
phrases.english: so it teaches us that it is not מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14 against רב פפא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the clause is needed to block a mistaken assumption (אצטריך / סלקא דעתך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the שור breaks out against one species, it is מועד for all of that species, big and small.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even within one species, a שור that is מועד for small animals is not מועד for large ones.

steps.title: רב פפא's proof from the clause about people and animals
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings proof from the clause 'מועד לאדם אינו מועד לבהמה'. Under his reading, this clause teaches a new point: even though goring an animal is more common, a שור that is מועד for people is still not מועד for animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא learns his view from the earlier clause, which says: one that is מועד for people is not מועד for animals. If we read 'is not מועד', then the default is that it is not מועד. The clause teaches that even from people to animals, the default is still not מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows how רב פפא proves his reading from the clause about אדם and בהמה, which fits his reading smoothly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב פפא, the default is that a שור is not מועד beyond what it has shown. The אדם/בהמה clause adds that this is true even though attacking animals is the more 'natural' next step for an ox. So the clause has real content under his reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Infers; draws a precise reading from the wording
The earlier clause of the משנה
It works out well; this side fits nicely
Ordinarily, by default, with no special evidence

steps.confusionAlert: The 'רישא' here is the clause 'מועד לאדם אינו מועד לבהמה'. It comes before the סיפא about small and large animals. It is not the opening words about מינו and שאינו מינו.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa infers from the earlier clause,
which teaches:
One that is מועד for people is not מועד for animals.
It works out well if you say
that we learned "is not מועד":
phrases.notes: This is about the opening words of the משנה: מועד for its own kind, "is not מועד" for other kinds.

phrases.english: then by default it is not מועד;
and this is what the clause teaches us:
that even going from people to animals too,
by default it is not מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב פפא, the גמרא spells out his positive proof, which was mentioned in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reading: 'אינו מועד' (a שור is not מועד for other kinds by default)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה clause 'מועד לאדם אינו מועד לבהמה'

steps.title: Under רב זביד's reading the people-and-animals clause would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה reads 'ואינו מועד', then by default a שור is מועד for other kinds. If it becomes מועד from one animal to another, then of course it becomes מועד from people to animals. So the clause would teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the משנה reads 'and is not מועד', then by default it is מועד. Now, if from animal to animal it is מועד by default, do we even need to say that from people to animals it is מועד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's proof by showing that רב זביד's reading would make the אדם/בהמה clause pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goring an animal is more typical for an ox than goring a person. So if a שור that gores one animal kind is מועד for all animal kinds, a שור that gores people would surely be מועד for animals. Under רב זביד's reading, the clause would be stating the obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say; sets up the other side to show it fails
Now that; begins a 'surely then' argument
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is obvious

phrases.english: But if you say
that it teaches "and is not מועד",
then by default it is מועד;
now that one can say:
from one animal to another animal, by default it is מועד,
from people to animals
does it need to be said that it is מועד?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's proof by showing that the opposite reading fails.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'surely then' argument (קל וחומר style): if animal to animal is מועד by default, people to animals surely would be. So the clause 'מועד לאדם אינו מועד לבהמה' would be pointless.

steps.title: רב זביד explains the people-and-animals clause as a case of the ox calming down
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the clause speaks of a שור that was מועד for both people and animals. It then stood near animals three times without goring. The משנה teaches that this reverting counts for animals, even though it is still dangerous to people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד would answer: the earlier clause is about reverting. For example, the ox was מועד for people and for animals, then reverted regarding animals: it stood near an animal three times and did not gore. You might think that since it did not revert regarding people, its reverting with animals does not count. So the משנה teaches that its reverting with animals does count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers רב פפא's proof by reading the אדם/בהמה clause as talking about a different case: an ox calming down (חזרה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד says the clause is not about whether being מועד for people spreads to animals. It is about a שור that was מועד for both and then showed calm behavior toward animals three times. The new point is that this partial calming works for animals, even though the שור stays מועד for people.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverting; a מועד ox returning to תם status
Three times
Gored
You might have said; introduces the mistaken thought the source rules out

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: a שור is מועד only for what it has shown, and the אדם/בהמה clause proves it. רב זביד: being מועד spreads to other kinds, and the אדם/בהמה clause is about an ox that calmed down toward animals but not toward people.

phrases.english: And Rav Zevid would say to you:
The earlier clause is about reverting,
for example, where it was מועד for people
and מועד for animals,
and then it reverted regarding animals,
meaning it stood next to an animal three times
and did not gore.
You might have said,
since it did not revert regarding people,
the reverting regarding animals is not a real reverting;
so it teaches us
that the reverting regarding animals, at least, is a real reverting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב זְבִיד אָמַר לָךְ: רֵישָׁא אַחֲזָרָה קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's proof from Steps 16 and 17 by redefining the case of the אדם/בהמה clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (אוקימתא): the clause speaks of חזרה, not of spreading מועד status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שור that is still מועד for people cannot revert regarding animals; its calm behavior toward animals does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reverting regarding animals counts on its own, even while the שור stays מועד for people.

steps.title: Objection from סומכוס: the first opinion must say 'not מועד'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes סומכוס: a שור that is מועד for people is מועד for animals, by a קל וחומר. This implies the תנא קמא disagrees and holds it is not מועד for animals. That fits רב פפא's reading and challenges רב זביד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: סומכוס says an ox that is מועד for people is also מועד for animals, by a קל וחומר. If it is dangerous to people, surely it is dangerous to animals! This implies that the first תנא says 'it is not מועד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב זביד. סומכוס seems to be arguing against someone who says an ox that is מועד for people is not מועד for animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס says goring people is the bigger step, so an ox that gores people surely gores animals. If he has to argue this, the other side (the תנא קמא of the משנה) must hold 'אינו מועד', a ruling that it is not מועד for animals. That matches רב פפא's reading, not רב זביד's 'ואינו מועד', which only describes a case.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
A תנא, a student of רבי מאיר
Logic from a weaker case to a stronger case: 'if this, then surely that'
By implication; this shows that
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Sumakhos says:
An ox forewarned for people is forewarned for animals,
by an a fortiori argument:
If it is forewarned for people,
is it not all the more so for animals?
This implies that the first tanna
is saying 'it is not forewarned'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב זביד explained the clause as being about reverting, the גמרא now attacks his reading with an outside ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's reading of the משנה as 'ואינו מועד'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סומכוס argues by קל וחומר that an ox מועד for people is מועד for animals. That implies the תנא קמא ruled the opposite, 'אינו מועד', which is רב פפא's reading.

steps.title: רב זביד: סומכוס is talking about reverting
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד reads סומכוס as talking about an ox that reverted. The תנא קמא says that if the ox stops goring animals, it counts as reverting for animals. סומכוס says that if it has not calmed down toward people, it surely has not calmed down toward animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד can answer: סומכוס is talking about reverting. He tells the תנא קמא: you say that calming down toward animals counts as reverting. But it does not count, by a קל וחומר from people. If the ox has not calmed down toward people, surely it has not really calmed down toward animals!
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד defends his reading. He says סומכוס is arguing about the reverting case from Step 18, not about whether the ox is מועד to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, רב זביד explained the משנה's case as an ox that was מועד for both people and animals and then stopped goring animals. The תנא קמא says this reverting counts for animals. סומכוס disagrees: an ox still dangerous to people (the harder target) is surely still dangerous to animals. So the ברייתא no longer proves the 'אינו מועד' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you: a defense on someone's behalf
Reverting: a מועד ox going back to being a תם after showing calm behavior
He is standing on (talking about) the reverting case

steps.confusionAlert: Here סומכוס's 'קל וחומר' runs in the reverse direction. He is not proving that the ox becomes מועד for animals. He is proving that its calm behavior around animals does not undo its מועד status.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid could say to you:
Sumakhos is talking about reverting,
phrases.notes: This is the case from רב זביד's last answer: an ox מועד for both, which then stood near animals three times without goring.

phrases.english: and this is what he says to the first tanna:
What you say, that reverting for animals is a real reverting,
reverting for animals is not a real reverting,
by an a fortiori argument from people:
If it has not turned back from people,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter מ in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so from animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב זְבִיד: סוֹמְכוֹס – אַחֲזָרָה קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 19 by reinterpreting what סומכוס is arguing about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the challenging source, using רב זביד's own case from Step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סומכוס argues that a שור מועד for people becomes מועד for animals, implying the תנא קמא said 'אינו מועד'.
steps.terutzMaskana: סומכוס is arguing about reverting. Calm behavior toward animals does not count as reverting while the ox is still dangerous to people. So there is no proof for רב פפא's reading.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes the case of an ox מועד for שבתות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a source to support רב זביד. In the משנה, the Sages ask רבי יהודה about an ox that is מועד for שבתות and not for weekdays. He answers: full damages on שבת and half damages on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear. They said before רבי יהודה: what about an ox that is מועד for שבתות and is not מועד for weekdays? He said to them: for שבתות it pays full damages, and for weekdays it pays half damages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes a case from the משנה that uses the same wording, 'ואינו מועד'. This step sets up the source. The actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point to notice is the setup: the Sages are speaking to רבי יהודה and he responds to them. That back-and-forth matters for the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source as proof
Days of שבת
Weekdays
Full damages, paid by the owner of a מועד
Half damages, paid by the owner of a תם

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear:
They said before Rabbi Yehuda:
This ox is forewarned for Shabbatot
and is not forewarned for weekdays, what is the law?
He said to them:
For Shabbatot, he pays full damages;
for weekdays, he pays half damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב זביד, the גמרא now brings positive support for his reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's exchange between the Sages and רבי יהודה about an ox מועד for שבתות

steps.title: A question and answer only fits 'ואינו מועד'
steps.stepSummary: With 'ואינו מועד', the Sages are asking a real question and רבי יהודה answers it. With 'אינו מועד', the Sages would be teaching רבי יהודה the ruling, and his answer would add nothing. So the wording must be 'ואינו מועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if the text says 'ואינו מועד' ('and has not become מועד'): they were asking him, and he answered them. But if the text says 'אינו מועד' ('it is not מועד'), were they teaching him the law?! And besides, what was he answering them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof. Only רב זביד's reading fits a conversation in which the Sages ask and רבי יהודה answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואינו מועד' describes the case, so the Sages are asking what the law is. 'אינו מועד' is already a ruling, so the Sages would be telling רבי יהודה the answer themselves. His reply would then teach nothing. Since the משנה clearly presents a question and an answer, the wording 'ואינו מועד' is supported.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if: this reading fits
Asking, posing a question
Teaching, telling someone the law
And furthermore: adds a second problem

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between 'ואינו מועד' (describing a case, which leads to a question) and 'אינו מועד' (stating a ruling) decides whether the Sages are asking רבי יהודה or telling him. Because the משנה shows them asking, רב אשי supports רב זביד's reading.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
it teaches 'and is not forewarned':
they were asking him,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and he in turn was answering them.
But if you say
it teaches 'it is not forewarned':
were they teaching him the law?!

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, אִיהוּ מַאי קָא מַהְדַּר לְהוּ?
phrases.english: And furthermore, what was he answering them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the source quoted in Step 21 proves רב זביד's reading.
steps.raayaObject: The reading 'ואינו מועד' in the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The question-and-answer form of the exchange with רבי יהודה, which fits only a descriptive 'ואינו מועד'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the form of a conversation in a משנה (a question followed by an answer) can decide its exact wording.

steps.title: רב ינאי finds support in the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: רב ינאי says that the earlier clause of the משנה also supports רב זביד's reading. He quotes that clause: whatever it is מועד for, the owner pays full damages, and whatever it is not מועד for, he pays half damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ינאי said: The earlier part of the משנה also shows this. It says: for what the ox is forewarned about, the owner pays full damages. For what it is not forewarned about, he pays half damages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ינאי opens a second proof for רב זביד. Here he only quotes the line from the משנה; his reasoning comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's proof (steps 21-22) came from רבי יהודה's case about שבת. רב ינאי now points to a different line in the משנה. He will show that this line only makes sense if the משנה reads 'ואינו מועד'.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier part of a משנה or ברייתא
It can be shown from a close reading of the words
Full damages, paid by the owner of an ox that is מועד
Half damages, paid by the owner of an ox that is תם

phrases.english: Rav Yannai said:
From the earlier clause too it can be shown,
for it teaches: that for which it is forewarned,
he pays full damages,
and that for which it is not forewarned,
[he pays] half damages.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof from a different clause of the same משנה, supporting the same conclusion as רב אשי.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's reading of the משנה as 'ואינו מועד'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The clause in the משנה: 'את שמועד לו משלם נזק שלם, ואת שאינו מועד לו משלם חצי נזק'.

steps.title: Why the payment line proves the wording
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה reads 'ואינו מועד', it is describing a case, and the payment line tells us what to pay in that case. If it reads 'אינו מועד', the rule was already settled, and the payment line would only repeat the basic law that a תם pays half and a מועד pays full.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if the משנה says 'and it is not forewarned': then the payment line explains the case. But if it says 'it is not forewarned', the משנה already gave the ruling. Then why add 'for what it is forewarned about he pays full, and for what it is not, half'? Didn't the משנה already teach us that a non-forewarned ox pays half and a forewarned ox pays full?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ינאי explains his proof. Only the reading 'ואינו מועד' gives the payment line a real job to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ואינו מועד', the first part of the משנה only sets up a case: an ox that is מועד for one thing and not for another. The payment line then gives the ruling for that case. With 'אינו מועד', the first part already gives the ruling, so the payment line would add nothing new. A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason, so the wording must be 'ואינו מועד'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining the case, not repeating it
It already settled the ruling
What more does it add?
An ox that is not yet forewarned; its owner pays half damages

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same words, 'אינו מועד'. The only difference is the letter ו ('and'). With the ו, the phrase is part of a case description. Without it, the phrase is a ruling.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that it teaches 'and it is not forewarned':
then it is explaining that case.
But if you say
that it teaches 'it is not forewarned', it already settled it;
what more does 'that for which it is forewarned'
he pays full damages,
and that for which it is not forewarned,
he pays half damages' add?
Until now, has it not taught us
that a non-forewarned ox pays half damages,
and a forewarned one pays full damages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the clause quoted in step 23 proves the wording.
steps.raayaObject: The reading 'ואינו מועד', which supports רב זביד over רב פפא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a משנה would not repeat the basic law about תם and מועד for no reason.
steps.whatToRemember: There are now two proofs for 'ואינו מועד': רב אשי's from רבי יהודה's case about שבת, and רב ינאי's from the payment line. Both use the same idea: only that reading gives every line of the משנה a real job.

steps.title: Three different species still make the ox forewarned for all
steps.stepSummary: Even if we accept רב פפא, who holds that an ox מועד for one species is not מועד for others, an ox that gored an ox, a donkey and a camel becomes מועד for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you say that רב פפא's view is correct: if an ox gored an ox, a donkey and a camel, it becomes forewarned for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes with a practical ruling. It holds true even according to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, being מועד for one species does not carry over to other species. Still, three gorings of three different species together count as three gorings. This makes the ox מועד for all of them, even though it did not gore each species three times.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you take the position that...
רב פפא's view is accepted
Forewarned for all of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit on רב פפא's view. Even according to him, the three gorings needed to make an ox מועד do not all have to be against the same species.

phrases.english: And even if you should say
that Rav Pappa's view stands:
if it gored an ox, a donkey and a camel,
it becomes forewarned for all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר נָמֵי אִיתָא לִדְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for רב זביד, the גמרא adds a ruling that holds even according to רב פפא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Goring three different species makes an ox מועד for all of them, even according to רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נגח שור חמור וגמל – נעשה מועד לכל.

steps.title: An ox that gores every other ox
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an ox which gores, skips, gores, skips, gores, skips among oxen becomes מועד in an alternating pattern for oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: An ox saw an ox and gored it. Then it saw an ox and did not gore it. Then it saw an ox and gored it, then an ox and did not gore it, then an ox and gored it, then an ox and did not gore it. It becomes מועד for oxen in an alternating pattern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new kind of pattern. The ox gores only every other ox, and this pattern repeats three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an ox becomes מועד by goring three times. Here each goring has a skip in between, so the ox becomes מועד for the pattern itself: the 'goring turn' ones, not the 'skip turn' ones. For the oxen in between, it stays a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
It gored
An animal with a proven habit of damaging; the owner pays full damages
In an alternating pattern, every other one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this ox is מועד for every ox it meets. It is מועד only for the ones that fall in the goring turn of its pattern, and still a תם for the ones in between.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: If it saw an ox, it gored;
an ox, it did not gore; an ox, it gored;
an ox, it did not gore; an ox, it gored;
an ox, it did not gore;
it becomes forewarned for alternate oxen.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רָאָה שׁוֹר – נָגַח, שׁוֹר – לֹא נָגַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of an ox that gored different species (Step 25), the גמרא turns to a new topic: an ox that gores in an alternating pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that gores every other ox three times becomes מועד for alternate oxen.

steps.title: An ox that gores every other animal of different species
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא teaches that the same alternating pattern across different species makes the ox מועד in an alternating pattern for all animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: An ox saw an ox and gored it. It saw a donkey and did not gore it. It saw a horse and gored it, a camel and did not gore it, a mule and gored it, a wild donkey and did not gore it. It becomes מועד in an alternating pattern for all animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same on-off pattern. This time each animal is a different species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox gored three different species: an ox, a horse and a mule. Because the goring was spread across different kinds of animals, the ברייתא says it becomes מועד in an alternating pattern for all species, not just for one kind. This fits Step 25, where goring several different species made the ox מועד for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Camel
Mule
Wild donkey
For all (kinds of animals)

steps.whatToRemember: An alternating pattern of goring makes an ox מועד for every other animal. If the pattern was all oxen, it is מועד for alternate oxen. If it was mixed species, it is מועד for alternate animals of all kinds.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ox's habit can be defined by both the pattern and the range of animals involved.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: If it saw an ox, it gored;
a donkey, it did not gore; a horse, it gored;
a camel, it did not gore; a mule, it gored;
a wild donkey, it did not gore;
it becomes forewarned for alternate animals of all kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רָאָה שׁוֹר – נָגַח, חֲמוֹר – לֹא נָגַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the alternating pattern from Step 26 and applies it to a mix of different species.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that gores every other animal across different species becomes מועד for alternate animals of all species.

steps.title: A new question begins about an ox that gored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question about an ox that gored. The rest of the question continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked before them: If it gored...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move, a new question that it cannot answer from a known source. Only the opening words appear here, and the question itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ signals a real question the Sages were unsure about. The word נָגַח shows it will again be about an ox's goring pattern, but the details continue past this section.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real question the Sages were unsure about)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them: If it gored

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two ברייתות about alternating patterns, the גמרא opens a new question that builds on goring patterns.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A further case of how an ox's goring pattern makes it מועד. The details are given past this section.
